title: Mechanisms of p53 core tetramer stability mediated by multi-interface interactions: A molecular dynamics study.
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过全原子分子动力学模拟解析p53核心四聚体多界面稳定性机制，并涉及p53与DNA的亲和力及关键残基氢键作用，属于蛋白质-DNA互作体系，但核心聚焦四聚体蛋白-蛋白界面而非TF-DNA结合位点预测或动态结合机理建模，方法为MD模拟，与本课题部分相关。
abstract: p53 is a tumor suppressor protein for impeding cancer development and maintaining genetic integrity. The formation of the p53 core tetramer is regulated by multiple cooperative interaction interfaces. To investigate the internal mechanisms of tetramer stability, we performed all-atom molecular dynamics simulations. Our findings indicate that the symmetric interface maintains highly conserved interactions, while the dimer-dimer interface displays notable flexibility. Additionally, we identified a novel salt bridge at the dimer-dimer interface that significantly contributes to the interaction energy. Moreover, the affinity of p53 for DNA is more than twice that of protein-protein interactions, driven primarily by five key residues that form multiple hydrogen bonds. Through independent simulations of the two dimeric models, we provide a theoretical explanation for why only the symmetric dimeric structure has been observed experimentally. The study identifies key regions and residues that contribute to stability at the inter-molecular interaction interfaces within the p53 tetramer, and highlight the important roles of each contact surface in the formation and stability of the tetramer.
abstract_zh: p53是一种肿瘤抑制蛋白，用于阻碍癌症发展并维持遗传完整性。p53核心四聚体的形成受多个协同相互作用界面的调控。为了探究四聚体稳定性的内在机制，我们进行了全原子分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟。我们的发现表明，对称界面维持着高度保守的相互作用，而二聚体-二聚体界面则表现出显著的灵活性。此外，我们在二聚体-二聚体界面识别出一个新型盐桥，该盐桥对相互作用能贡献显著。再者，p53对DNA的亲和力是蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用的两倍以上，这主要由五个关键残基驱动，它们形成多个氢键。通过对两种二聚体模型的独立模拟，我们为为何实验上仅观察到对称二聚体结构提供了理论解释。本研究识别了p53四聚体分子间相互作用界面中促进稳定性的关键区域和残基，并强调了每个接触表面在四聚体形成和稳定性中的重要作用。
